paragraphs: Swindon Borough Council runs its own fostering service, and the independent agencies shown above also approve carers who live in the borough. Fostering with the council means caring for Swindon's own children, usually close to their schools and families, with the council's social workers supporting you. An agency assesses, trains and supervises its own carers and offers homes to children placed by councils, including Swindon.

The need for local carers is the council's main message. In February 2026 the council leader, himself a former foster carer, said that in January the council was caring for 346 children with a cohort of only 73 foster carers, that 37 per cent of children in care were placed outside the borough, and that 130 Swindon children lived more than 20 miles away because there were not enough foster carers nearby. Ofsted's monitoring visit in June 2025 noted some progress in increasing foster placements but said more local carers are still needed.

The council's sufficiency strategy for 2023 to 2028 sets out who is hardest to find homes for: brothers and sisters who need to stay together, teenagers, parents with a baby, unaccompanied children seeking asylum, children with additional needs or disabilities, and children who need a home in an emergency or out of hours. At March 2023, 204 of the 338 children in care lived in foster homes.

The council offers short-term, emergency, long-term and respite fostering. Its statement of purpose says it contacts people who enquire within one working day, assesses in two stages with on average up to nine visits, and aims to finish within the eight months the regulations allow; its fostering panel meets twice a month. Approved carers have a supervising social worker who visits at least every six weeks, the Skills to Foster course and further training, at least three support groups a year, groups for carers' own children, and membership of The Fostering Network and the Swindon Foster Care Association. The council also lists discounted days out, use of a caravan at a Cotswolds holiday park and extra support for its own employees who foster.

We do not yet publish a Swindon pay page, so ask the council and two or three of the services above what they pay and how their support compares. The Wiltshire, Gloucestershire and Oxfordshire pages list more services nearby.
